_about: Everything the pack does not know. The Factory must not fill any of these by inference: each is resolved only by its named resolver, and the resolution is recorded. Status 'Resolved' records Isa's answer; residual questions stay open.

items.question: The pack's author has not seen the Factory's code.
items.resolver: Every card: its puller grounds the work in the code and cites files and commit; a seed whose premise does not hold is returned with evidence under R8
items.isa_answer: The institutions pull the cards and work as a collective; no named role pre-reads the code.

items.question: Current idea and card volumes.
items.isa_answer: Baseline from the analysis; measure live and improve. No study period.

items.question: Trial start date and duration.
items.isa_answer: No trial: build it, use it, monitor and improve (dog-food). Continuous monitoring (C0.15, C4.01).

items.question: Who holds vendor accounts and API keys, and how adapters obtain them.
items.status: Resolved in part (prototype: keys in the environment on Isa's own accounts)
items.resolver: The puller of C0.05 finds it in the code; confirmed in AR-10
items.isa_answer: The Owner; the keys are hashed in the Factory.
items.residual: [Inference] A one-way hash cannot authenticate an API call, so the Factory must also hold a usable credential, encrypted or in a secret store, and use the hash as a fingerprint. Confirm which is in place.

items.question: What a clean idea is worth.
items.isa_answer: Baseline each idea from the pack's analysis; replace with actual output. The Owner provides the actual costs paid in the real world.
items.decision: Unit USD. Cost: baseline from the cost model, actuals from metering plus Owner-entered invoices, subscriptions and cloud credits. Return: baseline from the idea's Alignment Record, actuals entered by the Owner.

items.question: Is Muse Spark 1.3 served to the Owner's account region (UK or KSA)? [Unverified]
items.status: Open (deferred to the pre-release gate; the prototype uses Isa's own accounts)
items.fallback: A second route (OpenRouter) and Gemini 3.8 Flash in the same class (docs/idea/value-stream.md §12).

items.question: No-training terms for every model tier used (R15), and their fit with Heliosvera IP.
items.status: Open (deferred to the pre-release gate; the prototype uses Isa's own accounts)
items.resolver: AR-10, with a qualified adviser where the terms are unclear

items.question: Three menu models have estimated Coding Index scores (Claude Opus 5.5, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-6 Luna).
items.resolver: Live evidence under R5 (promotion and demotion); re-run the model when Artificial Analysis publishes

items.question: Who owns live operation: incident, restore, hotfix.
items.isa_answer: Live operation must be part of the Factory.
items.decision: Until the Release Gate exists, incidents and restores are top-priority cards pulled by any agent and checked by another family (C0.16); then the Release Gate owns them (C2.03) [PROPOSED]. Hotfixes flow through the Market and Review.

items.question: Which ideas need Isa's ratification, and her weekly attention budget.
items.status: Resolved in part: no fixed weekly budget (Isa, 1 Oct 2026); the envelope's bounds and ceiling remain Isa's (AR-09b)
items.isa_answer: 1 Oct 2026: 'We do not need a ninth stage but definitely require self originated ideas. I disagree further briefs would load as that is a good problem to solve.' On the budget, 1 Oct 2026: 'do not worry on my weekly time budget as it can vary'.

items.question: Quality standards per institution and tier (maximum markdown rate).
items.decision: Baseline 1 minus the R19 floor per step [PROPOSED], adjusted from live variance.

items.question: Starting licence for menu models that are not in today's mapping. R11 says a new model starts at tier 1 and climbs by stretch cards; §5.1 treats the Artificial Analysis band as the starting prior. The Idea Record does not reconcile the two.
items.decision: [PROPOSED] Artificial Analysis band as the starting prior (§5.1), corrected by live evidence under R5; no replay spend.

items.question: Today's model roster, routes and predetermined mapping (R11 start state).
items.resolver: The puller of C0.17 records it from the Factory's code and records

items.question: Jurisdiction as a property of each route to a model: how data-residency law affects cost and efficiency.
items.status: Deferred (future); revisited at the pre-release gate (OI-21)
items.resolver: Future analysis; any legal reading needs a qualified adviser
items.isa_answer: Not an artificial single-country constraint; a future analysis.

items.question: Real vendor rate limits per account (the model assumed 8 instances per model, 48 in all).
Length of shadow periods and replay samples.
items.isa_answer: No shadow periods or replay: build, use, monitor and improve.

items.question: Key custody with aggregator routes.
items.decision: The self-hosted gateway (C0.19) keeps every key in the Owner's custody, hashed in the Factory. An aggregator route receives a vendor key only if the Owner registers one there; otherwise the route is not used. Terms reviewed in AR-10.

items.question: What must hold before the Factory becomes the system of record for other domains (replacing ERP, systems of record, mainframes): transactional integrity, retention, access control, segregation of duties, audit, jurisdiction, and a definition of a defect and deterministic checks per domain. Target architecture and load evidence: docs/idea/primitives.md (eight primitive stores; per-domain hash chains sealed in batches; crypto-shredding for erasure).
items.resolver: Design, then Isa; legal and regulatory reading by qualified advisers per domain
items.isa_answer: Eventually any person or team could set the Factory up for any kind of knowledge work.

items.question: Architecture for T3, high-throughput transactions (customer-facing, mainframe-class).
items.resolver: Design, when a domain crosses the T3 threshold on measured load; through the Release Gate
items.isa_answer: We do not need to solve the highest tier yet; T1 agent interactions and T2 systems of record run on Postgres and the current stack.

items.question: What must hold before user data enters the Factory for EvryMynd (user-owned sovereign memory and an agent council): ownership, residency of storage and processing, isolation between users, export, deletion, no training on user data, and counsel review per jurisdiction.
items.resolver: Design, then Isa; qualified advisers per jurisdiction
items.isa_answer: 5 Oct 2026: AI Factory is the intention; EvryMynd will eventually join with sovereign memory and an agent council for front-end users, carried by the Factory or through Cowork and similar interfaces.

items.question: Pre-release gate: what must hold before any user other than Isa (private testing under NDA, or release): consent and recording law in the UK, KSA, Morocco and the US states concerned; redaction at capture; vendor terms for speech and voice providers; where each route processes data; and whether anything touching health data may be recorded at all.
items.status: Deferred to the pre-release gate (Isa, 5 Oct 2026): the prototype has one user, Isa
items.resolver: Qualified counsel, then Isa, when private testing or release is near (draft brief exists: Consent and Recording: Brief for Counsel)
items.isa_answer: 5 Oct 2026: 'why have you gone down this route yet. Sequencing of this task comes when we are close to release ... This is not a live product with live users'
